fixes.explanation: Firstborn! I see where your head went, baker, because the Bible does talk about firstborn animals in other places. Not in this verse, though. Here God asks for "…an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats…" (Leviticus 22:19). Think of it as a recipe card with two lines: male, and no blemish. Skip either one and the whole batch is off.

A Nazirite? Ooh, that's a deep-cut guess, friend. You've been reading ahead! But this verse never brings one up. God says, "Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal." (Leviticus 22:25) So the rule reaches past the Israelites to the foreigner living among them. Nobody gets a special exception at this counter.

Canaan is where the Israelites were headed, so I get the mix-up, friend. But God is pointing backward here, to where He rescued them from. He says He "…brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) Canaan was ahead of them. Egypt was behind them.

BABYLON? Friend, that's a long walk from this passage! Babylon does show up later in the Bible, but it's way down the road from here. In this verse God says He "…brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) That's the rescue He wants them to remember, and Babylon isn't in the picture yet.
